records.expected: on a ready NATS 2.15.1 instance of revision 1.1.0 with JetStream, a connection without credentials that aims $JS.API.INFO replies at orders.evil and at the stream create, purge, delete, and message delete APIs leaves ORDERS with its one message and the stackly user with the one stream ORDERS; it is refused with Permissions Violation for every application, JetStream stream, system, and wide inbox subject; its _INBOX.stackly.> subscription never receives what the stackly user publishes there; and an empty password, a password for stackly-readiness, and an unknown user are refused with Authorization Violation
records.actual: NATS 2.15.1: 5 injected replies left ORDERS at 1 message, 5 subscribes and 8 publishes refused, no delivery across accounts, 3 foreign credentials refused

records.expected: behind the stacklyd binary with the default probe interval, a NATS 2.15.1 instance is created and ready through nats-readiness, a SIGSTOP turns readiness to not_ready with reason timeout while the port still accepts and the process stays running, SIGCONT makes it ready again, foreign servers give identity_mismatch, jetstream_disabled, jetstream_unexpected, and auth_required while matching ones succeed, an instance with JetStream off is ready without a jetstream folder, a SIGKILL of the daemon leaves the server running and the next daemon adopts the same process holding instance.lock, the stackly user signs in with its password while a wrong password and a connection without credentials are refused, two instances with a file stream ORDERS each keep only their own 3 and 5 messages, server name, store, password, and two loopback listeners across a restart, a file stream keeps its 10 messages across a restart while a memory stream is gone and the file stream is still there after SIGKILL, a held fixed monitoring port fails the start at endpoints with supervisor.endpoint_in_use and a suggestedPort while the instance stays stopped and the outside listener keeps working, the instance is ready on the suggested port, and a stop leaves no process
records.actual: NATS 2.15.1: ready through nats-readiness, not_ready with reason timeout under SIGSTOP and ready again after SIGCONT, foreign servers refused, adopted after SIGKILL, client password enforced, two instances isolated across a restart, file stream kept and memory stream gone after a restart, file stream F held 10 of 10 messages after SIGKILL of nats-server, monitoring port conflict refused at endpoints and ready on the suggested port, and stopped with no process left
